import pixeltable as pxt

# Get the existing videos table
videos = pxt.get_table('videos')

# Create a view that expands each video into one row per frame at 1 fps
# Using pixeltable's built-in frame extraction iterator
frames_view = pxt.create_view(
    'video_frames',
    select=[
        videos['*'],
        pxt.functions.extract_frames(videos['video'], fps=1).alias('frame')
    ]
)

print(f"Created view '{frames_view.name}'")

```python
import pixeltable as pxt

# Get the existing videos table
videos = pxt.get_table('videos')

# Create a view that expands each video into one row per frame at 1 fps
# Using pixeltable's built-in frame extraction iterator
frames_view = pxt.create_view(
    'video_frames',
    select=[
        videos['*'],
        pxt.functions.extract_frames(videos['video'], fps=1).alias('frame')
    ]
)

print(f"Created view '{frames_view.name}'")
print(frames_view.schema)
```
